Amazon.com, Inc.
Founded in 1994 by Jeff Bezos and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, Amazon.com, Inc. is a global technology and retail
leader. Driven by its core mission to be "Earth's most customer-centric company," Amazon has transformed from an online bookstore into one
of the world's largest e-commerce marketplaces and cloud computing infrastructure platforms.
Core Business Operations:
• E-Commerce & Retail:
Operates vast online storefronts and physical retail locations, offering millions of products directly and through third-
party seller partners.
•
Amazon Web Services (AWS):
Provides scalable cloud computing, storage, database management, and artificial intelligence solutions to
enterprises, startups, and governments globally.
•
Digital Services & Subscription:
Delivers digital entertainment through Prime Video, Amazon Music, and Kindle e-books, anchored by the
Amazon Prime membership network.
•
Advertising Services:
Offers performance-based digital advertising tools for sellers, vendors, and brand partners across its ecosystem.

• $5.3 Billion Global AWS Infrastructure Expansion:
AWS is investing $5.3 billion to launch its first
cloud region in Saudi Arabia by December 2026. The region includes 50 megawatts of dedicated AI
capacity and aims to upskill 100,000 citizens in cloud technologies.
• AWS Enterprise AI Acquisition:
In August 2026, AWS announced an agreement to acquire
DuckLabs (the team behind DuckDB) to strengthen its cloud analytics infrastructure and high-
performance database tools for enterprise customers.
• Record Financial & AWS Growth:
In its Q2 2026 financial results, Amazon reported $200.6 billion
in quarterly net sales (up 20% YoY), driven by an accelerating AWS cloud segment that jumped
37% YoY to reach a $169 billion annualized run rate.
• Peak Season Delivery Surcharges (2026
): Amazon Shipping introduced temporary 2026 holiday
delivery surcharges running from October 25, 2026, to January 16, 2027, ranging from $0.50 per
standard package up to $117.50 for large freight shipments.
